title: VinFast To Build Dedicated E-Scooter Assembly Line At TN Plant
summary: VinFast builds dedicated electric two-wheeler assembly line at its Tamil Nadu plant
detailed: Electric vehicle maker VinFast is building a dedicated electric two-wheeler production line at its Thoothukudi manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu.
The new escooter line is expected to roll out its first vehicles early next year and can reach a maximum capacity of 10 Lakh units annually.
VinFast Asia CEO Tapan Ghosh stated that the company received approval for the second phase of its broader $2 Bn investment in India.
The company is currently prioritizing its passenger car and electric two-wheeler businesses while deprioritizing electric bus plans for now.
sentences: Speaking with Inc42 on the sidelines of the company’s V Creator All Star Summit 2026, VinFast Asia chief executive Tapan Ghosh said that the manufacturer expects its first set of electric scooters to roll out of the plant early next year.
Anurag Saxena, the India CEO of VinFast’s escooter division, said that the two-wheeler production line is being developed independently of the existing car assembly operations.
While the company has not yet disclosed the initial capacity of the scooter line, Saxena said that the facility will be able to churn 10 Lakh units annually at maximum capacity.
However, the company does not plan to immediately invest in infrastructure to manufacture 10 Lakh scooters annually.
Ghosh said that production capacity will be scaled in line with customer response, market demand and the performance of individual product launches.
Besides electric scooters, the Vietnamese EV maker also plans to double down on its investments in India and is gearing up to expand its manufacturing footprint in the Southern state.
Ghosh said that the EV maker’s India arm has received approval for the second phase of its broader $2 Bn investment in the country.
However, he did not disclose the final investment outlay, the additional production capacity or the implementation timeline.
As part of this, the EV giant last year signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government for an additional 500 acres of land.
If materialised, the agreement will expand the size of its existing 450 acre Thoothukudi plant to nearly 950 acres.
The MoU, signed in December 2025, had outlined a proposed $500 Mn additional investment in the unit, which would pave the way for building dedicated production facilities for electric buses.
However, VinFast appears to be recalibrating its electric bus plans.
Ghosh told Inc42 that VinFast is not focusing on the electric segment for now, but is rather concentrating on scaling its passenger car and electric two-wheeler businesses.

He indicated that the company does not want to spread its resources across too many product categories simultaneously, adding that VinFast rather wants to adequately support the products it has launched.
VinFast commenced operations at its $500 Mn manufacturing facility in Thoothukudi in August last year.
The plant, spread across nearly 450 acres, was developed as part of the company’s planned $2 Bn investment in India.
The facility currently assembles VF 6 and VF 7 electric SUVs via the complete knock-down (CKD) route and has an installed annual production capacity of 50,000 vehicles.
For context, a CKD facility is simply a plant where components are assembled together into a full-fledged car.
Ghosh said that the facility was constructed within 17 months, with the initial investment directed entirely towards establishing VinFast’s car manufacturing infrastructure.
In addition, the EV maker has been steadily trying to increase its foothold in the Indian electric car market.
As per the Vahan data, VinFast registered 2,570 vehicles in October 2026, emerging as one of the top five electric passenger vehicle companies in India.
At present, its demand is driven roughly by personal electric vehicles, which drive 60% of its sales.
VinFast’s electric ride-hailing arm Green SM accounts for the remaining 40% of the sales.
Ghosh told Inc42 that the company retails about 1,200-1,300 cars through dealers every month, while Green SM buys about 1,000 more.
This translates to about 3,600 car sales every month at the upper end of the spectrum or about 43,200 registrations a year.
As such, VinFast’s current monthly sales remain well below its total installed capacity of 50,000 units annually.
But the Vietnamese OEM is betting on growing its dealer network and local assembly unit to carve a niche in the Indian EV market, which is projected to become a 132 Bn opportunity by 2030.
